the intercultural theatre event can be read as a cultural montage, and that this montage, when analyzed, can reveal aspects of the culture that is being presented, as well as the culture that is doing the presenting.
the ethnoscenological model is a useful tool to explore the cultural and theatrical ambiguities and contradictions that arise in intercultural performance events.
the intercultural theatre event can be read as a semiotic text, which can be analyzed in conjunction with the ethnoscenological approach.

how we might read intercultural performance, and how we might read it in a way that does not reaffirm the cultural hegemony of Western theatre practice.

the process of the textualization of the interculturalevent and how the spectator can be encouraged to explore and understand those aspects that are strange or unfamiliar, and how this can lead to the creation of a more inclusive and less ethnocentric theatrical event.

the ways in which the ethnoscenographic reading of the inter-cultural theatrical event can contribute towards the development of an inter-cultural theatre practice that is not simply a pastiche of cultural forms and styles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model allows for a more inclusive and less Eurocentric reading of the intertextual and intercultural performance event.
the ethnoscenographical approach to the intercultural theatre event, as outlined by Pavis, is an effective means of textualizing performance work that is culturally unfamiliar.

the spectator/critic is enabled to move beyond the limits of the Eurocentric and the Western gaze, to a point where they are able to engage with the cultural other, and to a degree, experience the otherness of the other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model for the analysis and interpretation of intercultural theatre performance.

the ethnoscenographic approach allows for the spectator/critic to explore the intercultural theatre event in order to create a textual montage that is culturally and historically specific and, in so doing, challenge the hegemony of the Western gaze.
the ethnoscenological approach to intercultural performance is one that is not only concerned with what is seen, but what is also heard, felt, and imagined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ethnoscenological approach to intercultural performance allows us to explore and analyze the theatrical event as a cultural phenomenon that has the potential for a transformative experience.
the intercultural event can be analyzed in a way that is both respectful of cultural difference and open to the possibility of cultural transformation.

intercultural performance, when analyzed through an ethnoscenographical lens, can be a site for the exploration and negotiation of cultural difference and otherness, as well as for the reconfiguration of the spectator/critic's own cultural perspective.
